claim: Follicular regulatory T cells (Tfr) restrict development of autoantibodies and autoimmunity while supporting high-affinity foreign antigen-specific humoral response.
source: Follicular regulatory T cells (Tfr) restrict development of autoantibodies and autoimmunity while supporting high-affinity foreign antigen-specific humoral response.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature establishing these roles of Tfr.

claim: Nuclear proteins contain antigens specific to Tfr.
source: Our study suggests that nuclear proteins contain antigens specific to Tfr.
evidence: This claim is based on experimental findings presented in the manuscript showing Tfr accumulation in response to nuclear proteins.

claim: Targeting nuclear proteins to antigen-specific B cells in mice triggers rapid accumulation of Tfr with immunosuppressive characteristics.
source: Targeting of these proteins to antigen-specific B cells in mice triggers rapid accumulation of Tfr with immunosuppressive characteristics.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing increased Tfr numbers and immunosuppressive gene expression after nuclear protein targeting.

claim: Tfr exert negative regulation of GC B cells with predominant inhibition of the nuclear protein-acquiring GC B cells.
source: Tfr then exert negative regulation of GC B cells with predominant inhibition of the nuclear protein-acquiring GC B cells, suggesting an important role of direct cognate Tfr-GC B cells interactions for the control of effector B cell response.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing greater suppression of nuclear protein-acquiring GC B cells compared to total GC B cells.

claim: Tfr play multiple roles in the regulation of B cell responses.
source: Tfr play multiple roles in the regulation of B cell responses.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Tfr prevent development of auto-Abs and autoimmunity.
source: On one side, Tfr prevent development of auto-Abs and autoimmunity (Botta et al., 2017; Clement et al., 2019; Fu et al., 2018; Gonzalez-Figueroa et al., 2021; Wu et al., 2016)
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: Tfr appear to have a modest negative effect on the GC and Ab response in some studies.
source: in some studies appear to have a modest negative effect on the GC and Ab response (Chung et al., 2011; Clement et al., 2019; Fu et al., 2018; Sage et al., 2016; Wollenberg et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Tfr affect B cell recruitment and selection in germinal centers.
source: In addition to that, Tfr affect B cell recruitment and selection in germinal centers (GCs) (Cavazzoni et al., 2022; Chung et al., 2011; Clement et al., 2019; Laidlaw et al., 2017; Lim et al., 2004; Linterman et al., 2011; Lu et al., 2021; Sage et al., 2016; Wollenberg et al., 2011; Wu et al., 2016; Xie et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: GC B cell responses critically depend on the provision of help by Tfh cells.
source: GC B cell responses critically depend on the provision of help by Tfh cells.
evidence: This claim is based on established scientific knowledge.

claim: Tfh cells differentiate from foreign Ag-specific Th cells following immunization or infection.
source: Tfh cells differentiate from foreign Ag-specific Th cells following immunization or infection.
evidence: This claim is based on established scientific knowledge.

claim: Differentiation of both Tfh cells and Tfr depends on the molecular interactions with antigen-presenting cells, involving SAP and ICOS molecules and the master transcription factor BCL6.
source: Importantly, differentiation of both Tfh cells and Tfr depends on the molecular interactions with antigen-presenting cells, involving SAP and ICOS molecules and the master transcription factor BCL6 (Hu et al., 2013; Johnston et al., 2009; Linterman et al., 2011; Nurieva et al., 2009; Pedros et al., 2016; Sage et al., 2013; Xu et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: Accumulation of Tfr in SLOs occurs at the same time or slightly after the Tfh cells.
source: Moreover, accumulation of Tfr in SLOs occurs at the same time or slightly after the Tfh cells.
evidence: This claim is based on established scientific knowledge.

claim: The Tfr TCR repertoire predominantly overlaps with natural FoxP3+ Tregs and is more diverse than the Tfh TCR repertoire.
source: However, in contrast to Tfh cells, the Tfr TCR repertoire predominantly overlaps with natural FoxP3+ Tregs and is more diverse than the Tfh TCR repertoire (Maceiras et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: TCR signaling must be important for Tfr development.
source: While some studies suggest that TCR signaling must be important for Tfr development (Maceiras et al., 2017; Shrestha et al., 2015)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Which self-antigens are cognate to Treg-derived Tfr is largely unknown.
source: which self-antigens are cognate to Treg-derived Tfr is largely unknown.
evidence: This claim is based on the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: There is very limited knowledge of the natural immunodominant self-antigens cognate to thymus derived Tregs.
source: Such analysis is further complicated by very limited knowledge of the natural immunodominant self-antigens cognate to thymus derived Tregs (Leonard et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: The deficiency in the identification of Tfr-specific self-antigens makes it difficult to assess whether Tfr may form direct cognate interactions with MHCII/self-peptides on the GC B cells.
source: The deficiency in the identification of Tfr-specific self-antigens makes it difficult to assess whether Tfr may form direct cognate interactions with MHCII/self-peptides on the GC B cells.
evidence: This claim is based on logical inference from the current state of knowledge.

claim: Tfr-produced membrane-attached neuritin has been shown to be acquired by B cells leading to their reduced ability to form plasma cells.
source: Tfr-produced membrane-attached neuritin has been recently shown to be acquired by B cells leading to their reduced ability to form plasma cells (Gonzalez-Figueroa et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: GC B cell-intrinsic production of CCL3 promotes direct contacts with Tfr and modest inhibition of the foreign Ag-specific B cells at the peak of GC response.
source: In addition, our previous study suggested that GC B cell-intrinsic production of CCL3 promotes direct contacts with Tfr and modest inhibition of the foreign Ag-specific B cells at the peak of GC response (Benet et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study by the authors.

claim: The contribution of direct Tfr-GC B cell encounters to the suppression of self-antigen-acquiring and potentially autoreactive GC B cells is not known.
source: However, the contribution of direct Tfr-GC B cell encounters to the suppression of self-antigen-acquiring and potentially autoreactive GC B cells is not known.
evidence: This claim is based on the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Tfr may restrict autoreactive B cell responses nonspecifically by reducing B cell activation/selection threshold through general inhibitory actions on B and/or Tfh cells.
source: The alternative hypothesis is that Tfr may restrict autoreactive B cell responses nonspecifically by reducing B cell activation/selection threshold through general inhibitory actions on B and/or Tfh cells.
evidence: This claim is presented as a hypothesis to be tested.

claim: Nuclear proteins often targeted by auto-Abs in autoimmune diseases include nucleosomal histones, SS-A/Ro, RNP-Sm, Scl70, and Jo-1.
source: NucPrs that are often targeted in autoimmune diseases by auto-Abs include nucleosomal histones, SS-A/Ro, RNP-Sm (small nuclear ribonucleoproteins), Scl70, and Jo-1 (aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase, both nuclear and cytoplasmic) (Mahler and Fritzler, 2010; Tan, 1983).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Tfr in the dLNs of SA-NucPrs-boosted mice were significantly increased as compared to mice boosted with SA or SA-OVA Ags.
source: We found that Tfr in the dLNs of SA-NucPrs-boosted mice were significantly increased as compared to mice boosted with SA or SA-OVA Ags (Figure 1A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A-C.

claim: The numbers and percentage of Tfh cells in the SA-NucPrs-boosted mice slightly decreased.
source: In contrast, the numbers and percentage of Tfh cells in the SA-NucPrs-boosted mice slightly decreased (Figure 1D and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D and E.

claim: The observed accumulation of CXCR5high PD1high FOXP3+ Tfr was not accompanied by increase in the frequencies of CXCR5int PD1int FOXP3+ or CXCR5low PD1low FOXP3+ Tregs.
source: The observed accumulation of CXCR5high PD1high FOXP3+ Tfr was not accompanied by increase in the frequencies of CXCR5int PD1int FOXP3+ or CXCR5low PD1low FOXP3+ Tregs (Figure 1B and F–H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B and F-H.

claim: TCR clonal repertoire of Tfr-like cells is very diverse, with majority of cells present at 1 cell per clone in the 10× data.
source: As previously reported (Maceiras et al., 2017), we found that TCR clonal repertoire of Tfr-like cells is very diverse, with majority of cells present at 1 cell per clone in the 10× data.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from 10× analysis and citation to a previous study.

claim: The majority of TCR clones in clusters 9–12 overlapped with TCR clones from other follicular T cell clusters.
source: Of note, the majority of TCR clones in clusters 9–12 overlapped with TCR clones from other follicular T cell clusters (Figure 2E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: In clusters 9 and 10 at least half of the clones were found exclusively in other Tfr-like clusters.
source: In clusters 9 and 10 at least half of the clones were found exclusively in other Tfr-like clusters.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from TCR repertoire analysis.

claim: In clusters 11 and 12 the majority of clones were also present in Tfh-like clusters.
source: In contrast, in clusters 11 and 12 the majority of clones were also present in Tfh-like clusters (Figure 2E and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E and F.

claim: Cluster 10 had the highest expression of Foxp3, Icos, Il2ra, Entpd1, and Ctla4.
source: In parallel to the observed accumulation of CXCR5high PD1high FOXP3+ cells in mice boosted with SA-NucPrs by flow cytometry (Figure 1C and F), 10× analysis revealed increase of cells in cluster 10 (Figure 2A and G) that had the highest expression of Foxp3, Icos, Il2ra, Entpd1, and Ctla4 (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1C, 1F, 2A, 2D, and 2G.

claim: Cluster 10 was enriched for cells expressing Il10 and granzyme B.
source: Cluster 10 was also enriched for cells expressing Il10 and granzyme B
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from 10× analysis.

claim: Nrn1 (encoding neuritin 1)-expressing cells were present in both clusters 9 and 10 and to some extent in other Tfr-like and Tfh-like cell clusters.
source: while Nrn1 (encoding neuritin 1)- expressing cells were present in both clusters 9 and 10 and to some extent in other Tfr-like and Tfh-like cell clusters (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1F.

claim: CXCR5high PD1high FOXP3+ cells with the highest levels of ICOS were CD25pos and had elevated levels of CTLA4, and granzyme B, as compared to Tfr with ICOSint/low and Tfh cells.
source: In accord with the 10× data for cluster 10, flow cytometry analysis confirmed that CXCR5high PD1high FOXP3+ cells with the highest levels of ICOS were CD25pos and had elevated levels of CTLA4, and granzyme B, as compared to Tfr with ICOSint/low and Tfh cells (Figure 2H–K).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2H-K.

claim: The accumulating Tfr in SA-NucPr-boosted mice are likely to have more immunosuppressive Treg phenotype.
source: Overall, the data suggests that the accumulating Tfr in SA-NucPr-boosted mice are likely to have more immunosuppressive Treg phenotype.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data showing elevated expression of immunosuppressive markers.

claim: There was no increase in the Tfh-like cell TCR clones within Tfr-like clusters in mice boosted with SA-NucPrs as compared to SA.
source: Importantly, we detected no increase in the Tfh-like cell TCR clones (from clusters 1–8) within Tfr-like clusters (9–12) in mice boosted with SA-NucPrs as compared to SA.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from TCR repertoire analysis.

claim: There was a trend for decreased frequency of Tfh-like cluster-associated clones among Tfr in mice boosted with SA-NucPr.
source: Moreover, there was a trend for decreased frequency of Tfh-like cluster-associated clones among Tfr in mice boosted with SA-NucPr (Figure 2E and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E and F.

claim: The observed increase in Tfr in the SA-NucPrs-boosted mice occurs due to accumulation of the cells with immunosuppressive phenotype that are not derived from abundant clones of Tfh cells.
source: Therefore, based on the 10× TCR immunorepertoire analysis, we suggest that the observed increase in Tfr in the SA-NucPrs-boosted mice occurs due to accumulation of the cells with immunosuppressive phenotype that are not derived from abundant clones of Tfh cells.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the TCR repertoire analysis data.

claim: Expression of proton-coupled peptide transporter Slc15a2 was completely abolished in SA-NucPrs-boosted mice.
source: For example, expression of proton-coupled peptide transporter Slc15a2 (that was detected in a few Tfh cells) was completely abolished in SA-NucPrs-boosted mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from single-cell analysis.

claim: The gene Apoe encoding apolipoprotein E was downregulated in the Tfr-induced mice.
source: In addition, the gene Apoe encoding apolipoprotein E (expressed in Tfh cluster 1) was downregulated in the Tfr-induced mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1H.

claim: In mice boosted with SA-NucPrs the frequency of GC B cells and the size of GCs were reduced compared to mice boosted with SA.
source: We found that in mice boosted with SA-NucPrs the frequency of GC B cells and the size of GCs were reduced compared to mice boosted with SA (Figure 3A and B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A, 3B, and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, B.

claim: SA-specific GC B cells underwent greater suppression than total GC B cells or DEL-specific B cells.
source: Moreover, SA-specific GC B cells that were expected to preferentially reacquire SA-linked NucPrs underwent greater suppression than total GC B cells or DEL-specific B cells (Figure 3A, C and D; Figure 3—figure supplement 1D–J).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A, C, D, and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D-J.

claim: In mice boosted with SA-OVA no decrease in the total or SA-specific GC B cells was detected.
source: Importantly, in mice boosted with SA-OVA no decrease in the total or SA-specific GC B cells was detected (Figure 3A–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A-D.

claim: Reduced accumulation of the SA-specific class-switched memory B cells was detected in mice boosted with SA-NucPrs.
source: In parallel to the observed reduction in the numbers of SA-specific GC B cells, we detected reduced accumulation of the SA-specific class-switched memory B cells in mice boosted with SA-NucPrs (Figure 3E–G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E-G.

claim: Decreased formation of SA-specific plasmablasts was found in mice boosted with SA-NucPrs.
source: We also found decreased formation of SA-specific plasmablasts (PB), including the PB recently derived from GC B cells (GCPB) (Figure 3H–L).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3H-L.

claim: In mice boosted with SA-NucPrs the titers of the SA-specific Abs were reduced as compared to mice boosted with SA.
source: Finally, in mice boosted with SA-NucPrs the titers of the SA-specific Abs were reduced as compared to mice boosted with SA (Figure 3—figure supplement 1K).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1K.

claim: The ratio of GC B cells to Tfh cells is elevated over fivefold in 6- to 8-week-old female NZM2328 compared to B6 mice.
source: In this study we found that the ratio of GC B cells to Tfh cells (that is highly conserved in GCs; Baumjohann et al., 2013) is elevated over fivefold in 6- to 8-week-old female NZM2328 compared to B6 mice, suggesting dysregulated GC responses even in young NZM2328 mice (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B and C.

claim: SA-DEL immunization followed by boosting with SA-NucPrs decreased the GC B/Tfh cell ratio in the NZM2328 mice, as well as in B6 mice.
source: Importantly, SA-DEL immunization followed by boosting with SA-NucPrs decreased the GC B/Tfh cell ratio in the NZM2328 mice, as well as in B6 mice (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B and C.

claim: The frequency of CXCR5high PD1high FoxP3+ Tfr in the Foxp3cre Bcl6fl/fl mice was low, and no increase in Tfr was observed after boosting these mice with SA-NucPrs.
source: As expected, the frequency of CXCR5high PD1high FoxP3+ Tfr in the Foxp3cre Bcl6fl/fl mice was low, and no increase in Tfr was observed after boosting these mice with SA-NucPrs (as opposed to Foxp3cre Bcl6+/+ control mice) (Figure 5A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A-C.

claim: While boosting Foxp3cre Bcl6+/+ mice with SA-NucPrs promoted significant suppression of the SA-specific and total GC B cells, both effects were completely abolished in the Tfr-deficient Foxp3cre Bcl6fl/fl mice.
source: Importantly, while boosting Foxp3cre Bcl6+/+ mice with SA-NucPrs promoted significant suppression of the SA-specific and total GC B cells, both effects were completely abolished in the Tfr-deficient Foxp3cre Bcl6fl/fl mice (Figure 5F–I).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5F-I.

claim: NucPrs-induced Tfr play a direct role in the negative regulation of the GC responses with predominant suppression of the NucPrs-acquiring GC B cells.
source: This data suggests a direct role of NucPrs-induced Tfr in the negative regulation of the GC responses with predominant suppression of the NucPrs-acquiring GC B cells.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data in Tfr-deficient mice.

claim: Direct immunization of naïve mice with SA-NucPrs did not induce rapid expansion of Tfr that was observed in mice preimmunized with SA-DEL.
source: Direct immunization of naïve mice with SA-NucPrs did not induce rapid expansion of Tfr that was observed in mice preimmunized with SA-DEL (Figure 6A–D, left panels).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A-D.

claim: No increase in Tfr and/or suppression of GC B cells was detected in mice preimmunized with OVA.
source: In contrast to the rapid expansion of Tfr and suppression of GCs in the SA-DEL-preimmunized mice, no increase in Tfr and/or suppression of GC B cells was detected in mice preimmunized with OVA (Figure 6B, D and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B, D, and F.

claim: Directing a combination of NucPrs to a selected subset of GC B cells may be a quick and efficient method for triggering rapid induction of Tfr and suppression of GC B cell subset that present the acquired NucPrs' peptides.
source: Since boosting of mice with an ongoing SA-specific GC response with SA-NucPrs is expected to promote acquisition of these Ags by the SA-specific GC B cells, we suggest that directing a combination of NucPrs to a selected subset of GC B cells may be a quick and efficient method for triggering rapid induction of Tfr and suppression of GC B cell subset that present the acquired NucPrs' peptides.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data.

claim: Robust increase in Tfr was detected in mice boosted with combined SA-NucPrs.
source: While robust increase in Tfr was detected in mice boosted with combined SA-NucPrs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Boosting with separate SA-NucPr Ags did not promote significant increase in Tfr.
source: boosting with separate SA-NucPr Ags did not promote significant increase in Tfr (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The observed increase in Tfr occurs due to additive accumulation of Tfr specific to various NucPrs Ags.
source: Based on this data we suggest that the observed increase in Tfr (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B) occurs due to additive accumulation of Tfr specific to various NucPrs Ags.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data.

claim: Decreased frequency of the SA-specific GCs B cells was detected in mice boosted with all selected Ags except SA-Jo1.
source: Despite the non-significant increase in Tfr after targeting separate NucPrs to SA-specific B cells, we detected decreased frequency of the SA-specific GCs B cells in mice boosted with all selected Ags except SA-Jo1 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Boosting of mice with SA-nucleosomes led to significant drop in the frequency and numbers of the nucleosome-specific GC and memory cells.
source: However, boosting of mice with SA-nucleosomes led to significant drop in the frequency and numbers of the nucleosome-specific GC and memory cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 1E–H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1E-H.

claim: Nucleosomes and other NucPr Ags contain peptides cognate to Tfr and if acquired by GC B cells may promote their suppression by Tfr.
source: Overall, this data suggests that nucleosomes and other NucPr Ags contain peptides cognate to Tfr and if acquired by GC B cells may promote their suppression by Tfr.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data.

claim: An increase in the frequency of Tfr-B cell conjugates was detected when Tfr were cocultured with activated B cells that have internalized NucPrs as compared to control Ags or B cells that did not acquire Ags.
source: In three independent experiments we detected an increase in the frequency of Tfr-B cell conjugates when Tfr were cocultured with activated B cells that have internalized NucPrs as compared to control Ags or B cells that did not acquire Ags (Figure 7B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7B and C.

claim: A significant fraction of the circulating human Tfr may be specific to the peptides from the NucPrs selected in this study.
source: Based on that, we suggest that a significant fraction of the circulating human Tfr may be specific to the peptides from the NucPrs selected in this study.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data on human Tfr-B cell conjugate formation.

claim: Combination of NucPrs induces rapid accumulation of Tfr in the dLNs.
source: In this study we showed that combination of NucPrs (SS-A/Ro, RNP-Sm, Scl70, Jo-1, and nucleosomes) selected based on their frequent targeting by auto-Abs in autoimmune diseases, induces rapid accumulation of Tfr in the dLNs.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: There is no detectable Tfr increase in mice directly immunized with NucPrs conjugated to SA and administered in Ribi adjuvant.
source: While there is no detectable Tfr increase in mice directly immunized with NucPrs (conjugated to SA and administered in Ribi adjuvant)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: A rapid Tfr response is detected when SA-NucPrs are administered to mice with an ongoing SA-specific GC response.
source: a rapid Tfr response is detected when SA-NucPrs are administered to mice with an ongoing SA-specific GC response.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Direct targeting of selected NucPrs to abundant antigen-specific B cells via BCR could be utilized to trigger very rapid and robust increase in Tfr.
source: it suggests that direct targeting of selected NucPrs to abundant antigen-specific B cells via BCR could be utilized to trigger very rapid and robust increase in Tfr.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data.

claim: The majority of the NucPrs-induced Tfr have distinct gene expression characteristics that suggest enhanced immunosuppressive functions.
source: Based on the 10× Genomics gene expression analysis, the majority of the NucPrs-induced Tfr have distinct gene expression characteristics that suggest enhanced immunosuppressive functions.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from 10× Genomics analysis.

claim: Tfr subset enriched in the SA-NucPrs-boosted mice (cluster 10) have significant clonal overlap with other Tfr subsets.
source: Based on the TCR immunorepertoire analysis, Tfr subset enriched in the SA-NucPrs-boosted mice (cluster 10) have significant clonal overlap with other Tfr subsets.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from TCR repertoire analysis.

claim: Tfr-like cell clusters 11 and 12 are predominantly overlapping with Tfh-like cell clones and may be related to the recently identified subset of Tfh cells in GCs that upregulate FOXP3 and play a role in the shutoff of GC response over time.
source: In contrast to this 'immunosuppressive' subset, Tfr-like cell clusters 11 and 12 are predominantly overlapping with Tfh-like cell clones and may be related to the recently identified subset of Tfh cells in GCs that upregulate FOXP3 and play a role in the shutoff of GC response over time (Jacobsen et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data and citation to a previous study.

claim: The majority of NucPrs-induced Tfr are not derived from Tfh cells.
source: Therefore, we suggest that the majority of NucPrs-induced Tfr are not derived from Tfh cells.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the TCR repertoire analysis data.

claim: Majority of NucPrs-induced Tfr accumulate due to proliferation of preexisting Tfr clones in the follicles or their precursors at the T/B border following their cognate interactions with NucPr-acquiring and -presenting B cells.
source: Based on this, on the previously established overlap of Tfr and Treg TCR repertoire, as well as the important role of Ag-specific B cells in the very rapid induction (3 days) of the immunosuppressive Tfr, we speculate that majority of NucPrs-induced Tfr accumulate due to proliferation of preexisting Tfr clones in the follicles or their precursors at the T/B border following their cognate interactions with NucPr-acquiring and -presenting B cells.
evidence: This claim is based on speculation from the experimental data and previous knowledge.

claim: Vaccine therapy with peptides from nucleosomal histones H4 and H1 promoted Treg response, diminished auto-Ab levels, and delayed the onset of nephritis in lupus-prone mice.
source: Vaccine therapy with peptides from nucleosomal histones H4 and H1 promoted Treg response, diminished auto-Ab levels, and delayed the onset of nephritis in lupus-prone mice (Kang et al., 2011; Kang et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Selected self-Ags contain multiple protein epitopes cognate to Tfr.
source: Because we detected the strongest Tfr response after administration of the combination of NucPrs, we suggest that selected self-Ags contain multiple protein epitopes cognate to Tfr.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data.

claim: Tfr induced by SA-NucPrs boosting promote partial suppression of the overall GC response.
source: Our data suggest that Tfr induced by SA-NucPrs boosting promote partial suppression of the overall GC response.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Tfr more strongly impede expansion of the SA-NucPrs-acquiring GC B cells and reduce their memory and Ab-secreting cell responses.
source: Importantly, they more strongly impede expansion of the SA-NucPrs-acquiring GC B cells and reduce their memory and Ab-secreting cell responses.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Cognate interactions with Tfr promote superior suppression of GC B cells.
source: Based on that, we conclude that cognate interactions with Tfr promote superior suppression of GC B cells.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data.

claim: The critical role of Tfr in the observed regulation is supported by complete reversal of the observed immunosuppression in the Tfr-deficient mice.
source: The critical role of Tfr in the observed regulation (rather than indirect effects from SA-NucPrs administration) is supported by complete reversal of the observed immunosuppression in the Tfr-deficient mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data in Tfr-deficient mice.

claim: NucPrs-induced Tfr upregulate expression of multiple genes that may potentially contribute to the negative regulation of B cells and Tfh cells, including Ctla4, Icos, Cd39, granzyme B, and Il10.
source: NucPrs-induced Tfr upregulate expression of multiple genes that may potentially contribute to the negative regulation of B cells and Tfh cells, including Ctla4, Icos, Cd39, granzyme B, and Il10.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from gene expression analysis.

claim: Expression of neuritine was not limited to the accumulating Tfr cluster with immunosuppressive phenotype.
source: Of note, expression of neuritine that was recently shown to be produced by Tfr and to limit B cell differentiation into plasma cells (Gonzalez-Figueroa et al., 2021) was not limited to the accumulating Tfr cluster with immunosuppressive phenotype.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from gene expression analysis and citation to a previous study.

claim: Multiple molecular mechanism may work in parallel to promote suppression of GC B cells.
source: We speculate that multiple molecular mechanism may work in parallel to promote suppression of GC B cells.
evidence: This claim is based on speculation from the experimental data.

claim: Cognate recognition by Tfr of the GC-presented MHCII/peptides likely leads to more prolonged interactions between the cells, increasing the duration of inhibitory signals received by GC B cells from cognate Tfr.
source: Cognate recognition by Tfr of the GC-presented MHCII/peptides likely leads to more prolonged interactions between the cells (Jacobsen et al., 2021), increasing the duration of inhibitory signals received by GC B cells from cognate Tfr.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data and citation to a previous study.

claim: SA-NucPrs boosting promotes a significant suppression of the NucPrs-acquiring GC B cells not only in the wild-type, but also in the lupus-prone NZM2328 mice that have dysregulated GC responses and over time develop anti-nuclear Abs.
source: To this end, our study suggests that SA-NucPrs boosting promotes a significant suppression of the NucPrs-acquiring GC B cells not only in the wild-type (WT), but also in the lupus-prone NZM2328 mice that have dysregulated GC responses and over time develop anti-nuclear Abs.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Targeting NucPrs to GC B cells should be further explored for analysis of their therapeutic potential for control of pathogenic B cells specific to autoantigens or/and allergens or promoting autoepitopes spreading for activation of pathogenic autoreactive T cells.
source: We therefore suggest that targeting NucPrs (and/or their specific peptides) to GC B cells should be further explored for analysis of their therapeutic potential for control of pathogenic B cells specific to autoantigens or/and allergens or promoting autoepitopes spreading for activation of pathogenic autoreactive T cells.
evidence: This claim is based on speculation about future applications of the findings.

claim: Tfr are a subset of regulatory T cells, predominantly CXCR5highPD1highFoxP3+, that are present in B cell follicles of secondary lymphoid organs.
source: Follicular regulatory T cells (Tfr) are a subset of regulatory T cells, predominantly CXCR5highPD1highFoxP3+, that are present in B cell follicles of secondary lymphoid organs (SLOs) (Chung et al., 2011; Lim et al., 2004; Linterman et al., 2011; Wollenberg et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Tfr deficiency leads to accumulation of anti-nuclear and tissue-specific antibodies.
source: Tfr deficiency leads to accumulation of anti-nuclear and tissue-specific antibodies (Abs) (Gonzalez-Figueroa et al., 2021), leading to development of auto-Ab-mediated autoimmunity in older mice (Fu et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The rise in Tfr is usually observed at the same time or slightly after the increase in Tfh/GC B cells.
source: Because the rise in Tfr is usually observed at the same time or slightly after the increase in Tfh/GC B cells (Aloulou et al., 2016; Turner et al., 2017a)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Bovine nucleosomes, SSA-Ro, RNP-Sm, Scl70, and Jo1 have over 92% homology to murine NucPrs.
source: Bovine nucleosomes, SSA-Ro, RNP-Sm, Scl70, and Jo1 (that have over 92% homology to murine NucPrs), were biotinylated and conjugated to streptavidin (SA) to generate SA-NucPrs.
evidence: This claim is based on knowledge about protein homology.

claim: While SA-boosting induced about threefold increase in the GC response as compared to no boosting control, no significant increase in GCs was detected in the SA-NucPrs-boosted mice.
source: Of note, while SA-boosting induced about threefold increase in the GC response as compared to no boosting control, no significant increase in GCs was detected in the SA-NucPrs-boosted mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: NZM2328 mice spontaneously develop dsDNA auto-Abs and systemic lupus erythematosus-like disease after 5 months of age.
source: NZM2328 mice spontaneously develop dsDNA auto-Abs and systemic lupus erythematosus-like disease after 5 months of age (Rudofsky and Lawrence, 1999; Waters et al., 2001; Wolf et al., 2018) and form anti-ribonucleoprotein (RNP) auto-Abs (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies and experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Human LNs have follicular T cells that resemble some gene expression characteristics of the immunosuppressive murine Tfr subset (cluster 10), but have reduced or undetectable expression of FOXP3 and express some factors typical for Tfh cells.
source: Therefore, based on the single-cell analysis, human LNs have follicular T cells that resemble some gene expression characteristics of the immunosuppressive murine Tfr subset (cluster 10), but have reduced or undetectable expression of FOXP3 and express some factors typical for Tfh cells.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the single-cell analysis of human lymph node data.

claim: About ~1% of GC B cells in SA-DEL-immunized mice boosted with SA were specific to nucleosomes.
source: In accord with previous study, we found (based on the staining with fluorescent nucleosome tetramers) that about ~1% of GC B cells in SA-DEL-immunized mice boosted with SA were specific to nucleosomes (Gonzalez-Figueroa et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and citation to a previous study.
